findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is unstable across processes
findings.body: cache_key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python string/tuple hash is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different web workers compute different keys for the same projects when cache is shared (memcached/Redis). Result is cache never hits cross-process (perf loss) and invalidate_upsampling_cache computes a different key than the writer in another process, so invalidation cannot work.

findings.title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns stale upsampled vs real counts
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60 seconds. If the project_allowlist option changes, queries within the window get the old decision and transform count() to upsampled_count() or vice versa, returning ~1/sample_rate inflated or deflated counts. invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere in the diff, so there is no way to close the window.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: Inside _get_event_stats the code calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the closure-captured dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover vs scoped_dataset for the same outer dataset, so _should_apply_sample_weight_transform sees the wrong dataset and can upsample transactions or skip upsampling errors.

findings.title: Discover-split queries bypass error detection because only request.GET is inspected
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query reads request.GET.get('query') while _get_event_stats builds split queries like f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction" in the query argument. An errors-only split on discover without literal event.type:error in the URL therefore returns False and skips the upsampling transform, undercounting by the sample factor. Conversely the check cannot see the actual Snuba query string being executed.

findings.title: Transform only handles exact count() and misses aliases/other counts
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites column_lower == 'count()'. yAxis values with aliases (e.g. 'count() as total'), extra whitespace variants, count_if/count_unique or equations pass through unchanged, so an allowlisted query silently returns raw sampled counts instead of upsampled counts when the frontend sends an aliased column.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with a comment assuming sample_weight exists for all events. Old/backfilled or non-sampled error rows have NULL/missing sample_weight, which sum skips, so those events contribute 0 instead of 1. Mixing sampled and unsampled rows undercounts; correct form needs coalesce/ifNull e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight,1)) or similar.

findings.title: Test helper sets sample_rate not sample_weight with swallowed errors
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate to normalized_data['sample_rate'] inside try/except pass blocks, with if client_sample_rate: skipping 0. The production aggregation sums sample_weight, so the test only passes if some other pipeline derives sample_weight from sample_rate; if not, the endpoint integration test asserting count==10 is testing the wrong column. Broad except also hides malformed contexts type errors.
